key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN models can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify process windows that avoid defects.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to optimize weld temperature, force, and defect formation while reducing trial-and-error in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE friction stir welding
Experimental validation across rotation speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating conditions
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series temperature and axial-force data
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental weld morphology and force/thermal trends.
watch_item: The process map and ANN generalization are limited to the tested HDPE parameter space, so extrapolation to other tool designs or polymers should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
